Answer: <one legal option letter>

Based on the chest X-ray in Figure 4, which of the following findings is most consistent with the diagnosis of bronchocentric granulomatosis, considering the clinical history and presentation? 

A) Presence of a homogenous mass at the left hilum with irregular borders, suggestive of malignancy.
B) Presence of a lobulated mass at the left hilum with smooth margins, indicative of a benign process.
C) Enlarged left hilum with a centrally located mass and evidence of bronchial obstruction, suggestive of granulomatous inflammation.
D) Evidence of calcification within the mass at the left hilum, suggestive of an old granulomatous disease.
E) Significant pleural effusion on the left side, suggesting an infectious process.
F) Presence of multiple small nodules throughout both lung fields, indicative of metastatic disease.
